headline: Goldman Sachs forecasts copper prices to reach $15,600 per ton by December 2027
hook: A bold long-term structural bull run
summary: Goldman Sachs has projected that copper prices will climb to $15,600 per ton by December 2027, driven by surging demand and supply constraints. The forecast highlights the increasing critical nature of the metal for global energy transitions and electrification. For Indian retail investors, rising global commodity prices directly impact domestic base metal producers like Hindalco and Vedanta. Sustained high copper prices can influence input costs for Indian electrical and manufacturing companies.
why_it_matters: Higher global copper prices boost earnings for Indian copper producers.
winners_losers: Metal producers gain / manufacturing cost rises

headline: Hindalco eyes valuation re-rating through capacity expansion
hook: Hindalco targets margin growth via value-added products
summary: Hindalco reported record revenue and profit for the September quarter, though management expects muted growth in the second half due to softer metal prices and rising input costs. The company is investing ₹50,000 crore in expansion projects to boost aluminium and copper capacity while shifting focus toward higher-margin value-added products. Novelis is transitioning from a capital-expenditure phase to earnings growth, with significant cost savings projected by FY28. The stock currently trades at a discount to its historical P/E average, suggesting potential for a re-rating if earnings momentum continues.
whats_next: June quarter FY28 for Bay Minette facility shipments
why_it_matters: Potential stock re-rating if value-added product strategy succeeds.
winners_losers: Hindalco shareholders gain / input cost suppliers hurt
